$comment: What 1 January 1936 was, written against the period and not against the scenario module. Where this and atlas/scenarios/gathering_storm.py disagree, one of them is wrong and somebody has to decide which.
sources: The interwar treaty network as it stood at the start of 1936: the Franco-Soviet pact of May 1935 and its Czechoslovak twin, the older French alliances with Poland and Czechoslovakia, the Little Entente, the Anglo-German Naval Agreement of June 1935, and Locarno -- three months before the Rhineland reoccupation tore it up. Sovereignty as of 1 January 1936: the Colonial Office and Quai d'Orsay territorial lists, the League mandates (A, B and C), and the Statute of Westminster's Dominions.

alliances.name: Franco-Soviet Treaty of Mutual Assistance
alliances.because: signed May 1935 and ratified in February 1936 -- the ratification Hitler cited as the pretext for the Rhineland. Modelled active because the era begins with it in the world.

alliances.name: Soviet-Czechoslovak Treaty
alliances.because: 1935, and conditional on France acting first -- which is why the two treaties have to be separate commitments rather than one bloc.

alliances.name: Little Entente
alliances.because: three parties against Hungarian revision, and pointed at nobody else -- which is the reason it does not help against Germany.

dependencies.name: Italian Eritrea
dependencies.because: an Italian colony since 1890 and the base the Ethiopian invasion was launched from.

dependencies.name: Italian Somaliland
dependencies.because: the southern pincer of the same campaign.

dependencies.name: British India
dependencies.because: one raj covering what became India, Pakistan and Bangladesh, plus Burma until April 1937. It was the largest single fact about British power and it was not a state.

dependencies.name: Mandatory Palestine
dependencies.because: a League mandate administered by Britain.

dependencies.name: Mandatory Palestine (the other half of the shape)
dependencies.because: the modern pack draws the mandate as two countries. Both are British, and this is the entry the auditor most needed: there was no Israel in 1936.

dependencies.name: Netherlands East Indies
dependencies.because: Dutch since the seventeenth century, the sixth-largest oil producer in the world, and most of why Japan looked south.

dependencies.name: Algeria
dependencies.because: three departements of metropolitan France, not a colony -- which is what made 1954 to 1962 what it was.

dependencies.name: Belgian Congo
dependencies.because: Belgian since 1908, and eighty times the size of Belgium.

dependencies.name: Italian Libya
dependencies.because: taken from the Ottomans in 1912 and declared an integral part of Italy in 1939.

dependencies.name: the Philippines
dependencies.because: a Commonwealth since November 1935 with independence promised for 1946 -- American sovereignty with a date on it.

dependencies.name: Korea
dependencies.because: annexed in 1910. The modern pack draws two Koreas and both are Japanese.

dependencies.name: South West Africa
dependencies.because: a C-class mandate administered by South Africa as if it were a province.

dependencies.name: Southern Rhodesia
dependencies.because: a self-governing colony -- London held the reserved powers, and the alternative invents a nation.

cores.because: a colony is held, not owned in the sense a core means. The test that once asserted Eritrea was an Italian core was codifying the bug: if a colony is a core, a peace settlement has no way to say it is being given up.

**the other 1936 finding.** Ireland was owned as British home soil, core and all. The Free State was a self-governing Dominion with its own army, its own constitution and a Statute of Westminster five years old -- not a British county.

the same rule the Italian colonies follow: a dependency is held, not owned in the sense a core means. If British India were a British core, a peace settlement would have no way to say it was being given up -- which is precisely the thing that happened in 1947.

leaders.name: Stanley Baldwin
leaders.title: Prime Minister
leaders.because: Baldwin returned in June 1935; Chamberlain does not follow until May 1937.

leaders.name: Léon Blum
leaders.title: Président du Conseil
leaders.because: a judgment call the scenario made and this manifest records rather than hides: Blum takes office in June 1936, and Sarraut holds it in January. He is seated because the Popular Front is the French position the era is about.

leaders.name: Edward Rydz-Śmigły
leaders.title: Marshal of Poland
leaders.because: Pilsudski died in May 1935 and the colonels' regime runs through Rydz-Smigly.

treaties.name: German-Polish Non-Aggression Pact
treaties.because: 1934, ten years, and repudiated by Germany in April 1939 -- so it must be a commitment the engine can report broken.

treaties.name: Anglo-German Naval Agreement
treaties.because: June 1935, bilateral, and concluded without France -- a limit agreed rather than a defence promised, which is why it is not a pact.

treaties.name: Locarno
treaties.because: in force on paper and untested in practice; the Rhineland is still demilitarised in January and will not be in March.

ungoverned.because: five overlapping claims, no permanent inhabitants and no government. The Antarctic Treaty is twenty-five years away, but 'claimed by several and governed by none' is much better modelled as ownerless ground than as a nation with a treasury and a border guard on the ice. All three eras now agree.

not_yet.name: Israel
not_yet.because: Mandatory Palestine; the state is twelve years away

not_yet.name: Bangladesh
not_yet.because: British India, then East Pakistan, until 1971

not_yet.name: India
not_yet.because: the Raj is a British possession, not a member state

not_yet.name: Myanmar
not_yet.because: Burma, and part of British India until April 1937

not_yet.name: Malaysia
not_yet.because: British Malaya and the Straits Settlements

not_yet.name: Singapore
not_yet.because: a Straits Settlement and the naval base the Far East strategy rested on

not_yet.name: Algeria
not_yet.because: French, and administratively part of France itself

not_yet.name: Namibia
not_yet.because: South West Africa, a South African mandate

not_yet.name: Jordan
not_yet.because: the Emirate of Transjordan, a British mandate

not_yet.name: Malta
not_yet.because: a British crown colony and fleet base

not_yet.name: Sudan
not_yet.because: the Anglo-Egyptian Sudan, British in practice

silent_on.organisations: The League of Nations is not modelled. It existed and mattered -- the Abyssinia crisis is a League crisis -- but Japan and Germany had left, Italy was leaving, and the body had no enforcement the `organisation` layer's veto arithmetic represents. A known gap rather than a claim that there was no body.
silent_on.occupied: Nothing begins under occupation. The Rhineland is demilitarised German ground, not held by anyone else, and that is the point of what happens in March.
silent_on.arsenals: No nation had a nuclear weapon in 1936, and the empty `arsenal` table is the correct world rather than an unwritten section.
silent_on.delivery: Nothing to deliver, so there is no boundary to walk.

doctrines.because: conscription and a reserve army of ~5m on mobilisation
Locarno, the Little Entente, the Franco-Soviet pact of 1935
a regular army of ~200k long-service volunteers; no conscription until 1939
the League of Nations, however badly it was going
joined the League in 1934; the Franco-Soviet pact in 1935
Montreux, and a policy of staying out that held until 1945
